item.title: Legislation to lower blood alcohol limit moves forward
item.description: Washington’s Senate voted 26-23 to approve legislation to reduce the maximum allowable blood alcohol concentration (BAC) for drivers from 0.08% to 0.05%. Sen. John Lovick, D-Mill Creek, a longtime Washington State Patrol trooper who later served as Snohomish County’s sheriff, introduced the bill. In 2023, the National Transportation Safety Board recommended that all states establish the 0.05% BAC. item.title: POLICE LOG
item.description: The Port Townsend Police Department (PTPD) logged 182 calls from Jan. 24-30. PTPD conducted 45 traffic stops, five of which resulted in infractions being issued, and arrested three DUI drivers. item.description: After months of uncertainty following the collapse of the Fort Worden Public Development Authority (PDA), Centrum has secured a long-term future at Fort Worden Historical State Park, signing a 35-year lease with the Washington State Parks Commission. item.title: Body of missing woman found in Olympic National Park
item.description: Search and rescue teams recovered the body of Alleacya “Angel” Boulia on Feb. 6 in Olympic National Park, more than two months after she was reported missing and her rental car was found abandoned at the Sol Duc Trailhead. item.title: D.C. bound
item.description: Members of the Chimacum High School Cowboy Marching Band perform in the rotunda of the Washington State Capitol building in Olympia the morning of Feb. 10. The performance marks another milestone in the band’s journey to Washington, D.C., this summer to march in the nation’s 250th anniversary parade. item.title: Voters approve school bond, fire district levies
item.description: The Port Townsend School District 2026 Capital Bond and both East Jefferson Fire Rescue’s (EJFR) levies passed by wide margins, according to preliminary special election results released Feb. 11.
